<h3 align="center">Castaway: menu disk 1992. One title on it, and it runs for ten hours.</h3>

<p align="center">
  <b>Ten hours, one palm, no hurry.</b><br>
  She sits on a very small island and nods to her headphones. Every so often something happens. Then she nods some more.
</p>

**Castaway** *(working title)* is a stationary-frame lo-fi video for YouTube, in the spirit of the ten-hour lofi streams: a young woman alone on a tiny island with one tall palm, a raft and a lot of time. She mostly idles. Every so often a message in a bottle washes straight back, a delivery drone lowers a parcel that turns out to be another pair of headphones, or a coconut lands on a hermit crab and the crab walks off wearing it. It is an unofficial remake inspired by the small-island routines and visual comedy of *Johnny Castaway*, the 1992 desert-island screensaver, repainted in a sunny, hand-painted coastal anime look: 16:9, 1080p at 24 fps, and always daytime.

More than 90 activities: most sit on four timers, from every few minutes to once in a few hours, and the rest only ever follow on from something else. Every one of them starts on the next bar of the music, so the gags land on the beat. Every sound is synthesized from code: no samples, no recordings.

<pre>
                THE LEEWARD LOT PRESENT: MENU DISK 1992, SIDE A

  1...WATCH HER WAIT: LIVE PREVIEW, MP4 EXPORT .............. <a href="tools/serve.py">tools/serve.py</a>
  2...TEN-HOUR SIM: CHECK THE SCHEDULE, RUN IT ........... <a href="tools/schedule.py">tools/schedule.py</a>
  3...SYNTH: EVERY SOUND, FROM CODE .................... <a href="tools/make_audio.py">tools/make_audio.py</a>
  4...DEV REEL: ONE OF EVERYTHING, WITH A HUD ......... <a href="tools/render_demo.py">tools/render_demo.py</a>
  5...THE SCHEDULE ITSELF .................................. <a href="activities.toml">activities.toml</a>
  6...THE RENDERER ITSELF ................................... <a href="web/index.html">web/index.html</a>

  0.......TOGGLE 50/60 HZ: NEITHER. IT IS 24 FPS, LIKE A FILM.
  SPACE...READ DOC FILE .......................................... <a href="MUSING.md">MUSING.md</a>
  M.......CHANGE MUSIC: THERE IS ONE TUNE. IT HAS BEEN CHOSEN FOR YOU.
</pre>

To load, from the project root:

```sh
python tools/serve.py
# then open http://127.0.0.1:8765/
```

The page plays a live preview and exports a YouTube-ready MP4. In development: no video has been published yet, so for now the only way to watch her wait is to run it.

<details>
<summary><b>SPACE</b>: read doc file (what happens, and how often)</summary>

```text
 ======================================================================
  CASTAWAY.DOC                                   MENU DISK 1992, SIDE A
 ======================================================================

  THE TIMERS        GOES OFF EVERY      IN A TYPICAL TEN-HOUR RUN
  REGULAR ......... 2 to 5 minutes .... about 155
  OCCASIONAL ...... 12 to 25 minutes .. about 30
  RARE ............ 30 to 60 minutes .. about 13
  SUPER RARE ...... 3 to 6 hours ...... about 2, never more than 3
  FOLLOW-UPS ...... only ever after something else
  IDLE ............ the other two thirds of the time. nodding.

  ON THE ISLAND, NOW AND THEN
  * a message in a bottle washes straight back. hours later, a
    different bottle brings a reply
  * a delivery drone lowers a parcel. inside: more headphones
  * a sea turtle swims in and dozes off beside her
  * a grey tabby with a white chest drifts in on a crate, climbs
    the palm, naps, and one day floats off again. it comes back
  * the signal hunt: one bar, at the very top of the palm
  * a shark surfaces in headphones and nods to the beat
  * a tour boat of selfie-takers
  * a coconut falls on a hermit crab. the crab keeps it
  * a bro on an electric hydrofoil gives a shaka and carves off
  * she plants a kumara, and it grows over the course of the video
  * bushcraft: fire by friction, a hammock, a lookout up the palm,
    spear fishing
  * "she could leave any time": she walks out over the water and
    comes back with an iced coffee
  * and in between: a coconut, some fishing, laps of the island, a
    sandcastle for the tide, a wave at the horizon, just in case
```

The counts are the median of 200 simulated runs, as the header of [activities.toml](activities.toml) says. Lanes let things overlap, so the world carries on while she is busy: a ship can sail past behind her while she is deep in a coconut. Every start waits for the next bar of the music, every 3 seconds. The default run is 10:00:00 with seed 1992, which is where this disk gets its number; `python tools/schedule.py` checks the file and simulates a run.

In the banner, the bottle comes back every 24 seconds. In the video it waits its turn on the occasional timer, which it shares with a lot of other things, so in some ten-hour runs it never comes round at all. That is not a bug. That is the island.

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>M</b>: change music (there is one tune, and it is a good sport about it)</summary>

- **All of it is code.** Every sound is synthesized by [tools/make_audio.py](tools/make_audio.py): no samples, no stock loops, no recordings, so no third-party licence applies. More than 150 sound files as of 2026-10-01, and counting.
- **The tune.** A seamless 60-second loop at 80 BPM in F major (ii-V-I-vi), 20 bars of exactly 3 seconds: electric piano, a kalimba lead, soft drums and vinyl crackle. Ten hours is six hundred laps of it, which is why pressing M changes nothing. The plan for more, in [MUSING.md](MUSING.md), is to change the script's seed, key, tempo or progression; for now there is the one.
- **The sea.** The ocean ambience is a seamless 60-second loop too. The mix sits at -14 LUFS with true peak at or below -1 dBTP, and levels are adjustable in master and per routine.
- **The honest bit.** Nobody has listened to any of it yet. It has been measured for loudness, clipping and loop seams, which is not the same as being heard.
- **The beat.** One bar is 3 seconds, so the banner keeps time too: the rasters roll one full red-to-black-and-back cycle per bar, the logo sways once per bar, and her head dips on every beat (80 BPM is one beat every 0.75 seconds).

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>0</b>: toggle 50/60 Hz (the picture and the machinery)</summary>

- **The picture.** Sunny, hand-painted coastal anime, 16:9, rendered at 1080p and 24 fps. Always daytime: that is a project rule. Hard cuts and stepped movement are the motion defaults. Scene life has 26 entries: shore waves and drifting cloud shadows are built; distant birds, planes with vapour trails, whale pods, dolphins, sailboats, sandpipers, a gecko and a rain shower are planned.
- **The renderer.** A web page, [web/index.html](web/index.html), with live preview and export: it encodes frame-exact H.264 in the browser with WebCodecs (measured at 68 to 78 frames a second at 1080p in Chrome), and the server mixes the sound and joins the two into an MP4. Plain ES modules, no build step, no npm packages.
- **The dev reel.** `python tools/render_demo.py --dev` renders a reel of every activity with a heads-up display, from the older Python reference renderer.
- **The 50/60 Hz key.** On the ST it switched the screen's refresh rate. Here the answer is 24 fps whichever key you press: a film rate, picked so each of her painted poses (12 a second) gets exactly two frames. You are encouraged to press none of them.

</details>

<details>

The Leeward Lot, its members and everyone it greets in capitals are invented, and so is the disk. The banner is drawn by a script, pixel by pixel: the slab logo, both fonts and the island picture are original, and no group's logo, font or graphics are copied. The style is a nod to the menu screens that UK crews put in front of Atari ST compilation floppies around 1988 to 1991: a key list, rolling rasters, a dithered picture and a big scroller. The only thing on this disk is this project.

</details>

<h1 align="center">Castaway</h1>

<p align="center">
  <b>Twenty tracks. Track 13 is one footstep on water, three tenths of a second long. Track 20 is ten hours long, and in it, mostly, she nods.</b><br>
  <sub>working title &middot; in development, nothing published yet &middot; an unofficial remake inspired by the 1992 screensaver <i>Johnny Castaway</i></sub>
</p>

**Castaway** is a stationary-frame lo-fi video for YouTube, in the spirit of the ten-hour lofi streams: a young woman alone on a tiny island with one tall palm, a raft and a lot of time. She mostly idles, nodding along to her headphones, and every so often something happens. A bottle she sends off washes straight back. A drone delivers a parcel, and the parcel is another pair of headphones. A coconut lands on a hermit crab, then walks off with the crab wearing it. She could leave any time: she strolls out over the water and comes back with an iced coffee. It is an unofficial remake inspired by the small-island routines and visual comedy of *Johnny Castaway*, painted as a sunny coastal anime scene: 16:9, 1080p, 30 fps, and always daytime.

What happens, and when, lives in [activities.toml](activities.toml): more than 90 activities. Four timers pick most of them, regular (every 2 to 5 minutes), occasional (12 to 25), rare (30 to 60) and super rare (every 3 to 6 hours, three at most), and the rest are follow-ups that only happen after something else has. A typical ten-hour run comes to about 155 regular, 30 occasional, 13 rare and 2 super-rare events, plus chained follow-ups. She is busy about a third of the time. The rest is the main feature. Every activity starts on the next bar of the music, every 3 seconds, so each gag lands on the beat.

**Every sound is synthesized from code** by [tools/make_audio.py](tools/make_audio.py): no samples, loops or recordings, so no third-party licence applies. There are more than 150 sound files so far. The jukebox up there lists nineteen of them, at their real running times, and then the whole video as track 20. The theme is a seamless 60-second loop at 80 BPM in F major (ii-V-I-vi), 20 bars of exactly 3 seconds, on electric piano, a kalimba lead, soft drums and vinyl crackle; the ocean is a seamless 60-second loop too. The mix sits at -14 LUFS with true peak at or below -1 dBTP, and levels can be set on the master and per routine. Nobody has heard any of it yet, so the jukebox can only tell you how long things are.

<p align="center">
  <kbd>S</kbd> start the stage &nbsp;&middot;&nbsp; <kbd>T</kbd> test the timers &nbsp;&middot;&nbsp; <kbd>A</kbd> make the audio again &nbsp;&middot;&nbsp; <kbd>D</kbd> dev reel &nbsp;&middot;&nbsp; <kbd>W</kbd> wait ten hours
</p>

```sh
python tools/serve.py               # S: then open http://127.0.0.1:8765/
python tools/schedule.py            # T: check the schedule, simulate 10 hours
python tools/make_audio.py          # A: every sound, from code (numpy + ffmpeg)
python tools/render_demo.py --dev   # D: every activity in a row, with a HUD
```

The page at <b>http://127.0.0.1:8765/</b> is the renderer: a live preview, and an export to a YouTube-ready MP4. Plain ES modules, no build step, no npm packages. It encodes frame-exact video in the browser (WebCodecs H.264, 68 to 78 frames a second at 1080p30 in Chrome), and the server mixes in the sound and joins the two. The default run is 10:00:00 on seed 1992. <kbd>W</kbd> needs no command.

<summary><b>Liner notes</b></summary>

- **Performed by:** tools/make_audio.py. **Recorded:** never. **Studio:** none. **Microphones:** none.
- **Instruments:** electric piano, kalimba, soft drums and vinyl crackle, all of them maths.
- **Longest track:** the video itself, 10:00:00. The 60-second theme fits in it 600 times.
- **Shortest track in the library:** one bare foot on sand, 0:00.2.
- **Requests:** not taken. The timers decide.
- **The panel:** the Jetsam Jukebox, after the chip-music jukebox screens of late-80s Atari ST and Amiga music disks. Everything on it is drawn from scratch by a Node script: letters, studs, island and all.

</details>

<sub>The Jetsam Jukebox does not exist. The sounds, their running times and the ten hours do. Castaway is an unofficial remake inspired by <i>Johnny Castaway</i> (1992), which belongs to its owners.</sub>

**Castaway** (working title) is a ten-hour lo-fi video for YouTube in which almost nothing happens, on purpose: one young woman, one tiny island, one tall palm, one raft and a great deal of time. Mostly she idles in cream headphones, nodding to the music. It is an unofficial remake inspired by the small-island routines and visual comedy of the 1992 screensaver *Johnny Castaway*, done sunny and hand-painted in a coastal anime look: 16:9 at 1080p, and always daytime.

Every so often, on the next bar of the music, something happens. More than 90 activities live in [activities.toml](activities.toml), most of them on four timers, from everyday things every few minutes (a spot of fishing, a sandcastle) to a super-rare stroll out across the water and back with an iced coffee: she could leave any time. In between, a bottle washes straight back, a drone delivers more headphones, a hermit crab walks off wearing a coconut and a shark in headphones nods along. A ship goes by as well. It makes no sound, and her eyes are shut.

Every sound is synthesized from code by [tools/make_audio.py](tools/make_audio.py): no samples, loops or recordings, so no third-party licence applies. That left the sample list with nothing to hold, so it took messages instead.

```sh
python tools/serve.py      # then open http://127.0.0.1:8765/
```

The page plays the run live and exports a YouTube-ready MP4: the browser encodes frame-exact H.264 and the server mixes in the sound. Plain ES modules, no build step, no npm packages.

<p><sub>In development: no video has been published yet, and nobody has heard the sound. Both are on the list.</sub></p>

<details>
<summary><b>how to read the list</b>: two lists, 31 slots each, 22 characters a slot</summary>

<br>

A tracker module keeps a name for each of its 31 samples, 22 characters apiece, and players showed those names to whoever was listening. So people wrote in them: messages centred by hand, lines starting with `#`, rules made of punctuation, greetings at the bottom, and between them the actual samples. Later modules added an instrument list beside it. This one is Castaway's.

- **Instruments are the gags.** Every activity starts on the next bar of the music, so the schedule plays them like notes. Each name is a real activity id from [activities.toml](activities.toml), with its timer as the disk prefix: `reg` every 2 to 5 minutes, `occ` every 12 to 25, `rare` every 30 to 60, `super` every 3 to 6 hours.
- **Samples are the sounds.** Castaway has none, so each slot holds the Python function that makes a sound for the gag beside it, cut at 22 characters like any long sample name. `len` is the real length of the file it writes, in frames at 48 kHz. Messages are 0 frames long, as they always were.
- **Slot 24 is empty on purpose.** The ship that sails past while she is busy cues no sound at all. She would not hear it anyway: headphones.
- **CAST and AWAY** are drawn in block pixels, one word per list, and so is the picture: she is in one list and the ship is in the other.

</details>

<h1 align="center">Castaway</h1>

<p align="center">
  <b>A ten-hour lo-fi island video, scored mostly in rests.</b><br>
  <sub>working title · in development, nothing published yet · an unofficial remake inspired by the 1992 screensaver <i>Johnny Castaway</i></sub>
</p>

**Castaway** is a stationary-frame lo-fi video for YouTube, in the spirit of the ten-hour lofi streams: a young woman alone on a tiny island with one tall palm, a raft, a pair of cream headphones and a great deal of time. She sits in the shade and nods to the music. Every so often, always on the next bar, something happens. A bottle she throws washes straight back to her feet. A drone delivers a parcel, and the parcel is another pair of headphones. A coconut lands on a hermit crab, and the crab walks off wearing it. Then she goes back to nodding, which is the main event. Sunny and hand-painted, 16:9, 1080p at 30 fps, and always daytime.

The screen up there is one minute of it, a busy one, written out as a module. Channels 0 to 3 are the theme, and the keys, kalimba and drums are its real notes, copied out of [tools/make_audio.py](tools/make_audio.py) onto the grid. Channels 4 to 7 are the island, and they are mostly dots, because the island is mostly waiting. This minute, a shark in headphones circles for nine bars, surfaces, and nods along with her on every beat for six more. The cat sleeps through it in the palm. The turtle is elsewhere. The ocean plays one note at 00:00:00 and leaves it running for the rest of the minute. Somebody keeps clicking Nod.

[activities.toml](activities.toml) is the instrument list: more than 90 activities, each on one of four timers. Regular ones come round every 2 to 5 minutes, occasional every 12 to 25, rare every 30 to 60, and super rare every 3 to 6 hours, three at most per run. In a typical ten-hour run (the median of 200 simulated ones) that comes to about 155 regular, 30 occasional, 13 rare and 2 super-rare events, plus chained follow-ups. She is busy about a third of the time. The other two thirds are the dots.

Every sound is synthesized from code by [tools/make_audio.py](tools/make_audio.py): no samples, loops or recordings, so no third-party licence applies, and the sample list is a list of things arithmetic made. The theme is a seamless 60-second loop at 80 BPM in F major (ii-V-I-vi), 20 bars of exactly 3 seconds, with electric piano, a kalimba lead, soft drums and vinyl crackle. The ocean is another seamless minute, and there are more than 150 sound files in all. The mix sits at -14 LUFS with true peak at or below -1 dBTP, and the levels can be set for the master and per routine. Nobody has listened to any of it yet. The scopes are drawn, not measured, so they have no opinion either.

```sh
python tools/serve.py               # then open http://127.0.0.1:8765/
python tools/schedule.py            # validate the schedule, simulate 10 hours
python tools/render_demo.py --dev   # a dev reel of every activity, with a HUD
```

<p><sub>The page at <a href="web/index.html">web/index.html</a> previews live and exports a YouTube-ready MP4: frame-exact H.264 encoded in the browser with WebCodecs (68 to 78 frames a second at 1080p30 in Chrome), then the server mixes in the sound and joins the two. Plain ES modules, no build step, no npm packages. <code>render_demo.py</code> is the older Python reference renderer. Hard cuts and stepped movement are the motion defaults, and the default run is 10:00:00 on seed 1992: same seed, same schedule.</sub></p>

On the left, a daylight pixel picture of the island: blue sky in stepped bands, a pale sun, small clouds drifting left, and a calm blue sea with glints that swap on the beat. One tall, slender palm with a segmented reddish-tan trunk leans over the sand, a grey tabby cat asleep in its fronds with a small z rising. In the palm's shade a young woman with brown hair and cream headphones, in a coral tank top and cream shorts, sits and nods on every beat. </p>

Patterns, plate and pixels by **Fermata**, who does not exist. A fermata is the sign over a note that says hold it as long as you like, which is the whole plan.

Greetings, on the beat, to the shark, for perfect timing; the cat, for sleeping through it; the turtle, for taking the minute off; the hermit crab and its new coconut; the bottle that came back; the drone and its spare headphones; the e-foil bro; and the ship, which would have been in this pattern, but the sea lane was busy.

<sub>Fermata and its tracker do not exist. The screen is drawn in the manner of mid-1990s DOS GUI trackers, and no real tracker's name, logo or screen is reproduced. The notes on channels 0 to 2 are the theme's own, transcribed from tools/make_audio.py and snapped to the grid: the real thing swings a little late on the off-beats, and its hats and bass are left out. The routine's durations and the file names are the project's own too; which channel each part of the routine sits in is staged for this minute. Castaway is an unofficial remake inspired by <i>Johnny Castaway</i> (1992), which belongs to its owners.</sub>

</details>

<h1 align="center">Castaway</h1>

<p align="center">
  <b>A ten-hour lo-fi island video, scored like a tracker module in which almost every cell is empty. On purpose.</b><br>
  <sub>working title · in development, nothing published yet · an unofficial remake inspired by the 1992 screensaver <i>Johnny Castaway</i></sub>
</p>

**Castaway** is a stationary-frame lo-fi video for YouTube, in the spirit of the ten-hour lofi streams: a young woman alone on a tiny island with one tall palm, a raft and a lot of time. She mostly idles, nodding to the music on her headphones, and every so often something happens. A bottle she throws washes straight back. A drone delivers a parcel, and the parcel is another pair of headphones. A stray cat drifts in on a crate and falls asleep up the palm. Sunny, hand-painted coastal anime, 16:9 at 1080p, and always daytime.

Read it as a module and it makes perfect sense. Eight channels: her, the cat, the turtle, the sea and sky, the shore and the garden (the six lanes in [`activities.toml`](activities.toml)), plus the theme and the ocean. One row per beat at 80 BPM. Every activity waits for the next bar, so every gag lands on the beat, and nearly every cell is a dot, because in a tracker a dot means nothing happens. Nothing happening is the song. In the minute up there, channel 01 gets up, walks off over the water, stays away for 27 rows and comes back with an iced coffee. The song does not notice. More than 90 activities, most of them on four timers, decide when the dots stop, and every sound is synthesized from code, so the sample memory reads 0k. That is accurate.

```
python tools/serve.py
```

Then open `http://127.0.0.1:8765/` for the live preview and the export to a YouTube-ready MP4: the browser encodes the frames, and the server mixes in the sound and joins the two. Plain ES modules, no build step, no npm packages.

<pre>
 Key .... Does .......................... Type this
 F1 ..... <a href="MUSING.md">Help, and what was decided</a> .... MUSING.md
 F5 ..... <a href="tools/serve.py">Play, preview, export</a> ......... python tools/serve.py
 F6 ..... <a href="tools/schedule.py">Check and simulate ten hours</a> .. python tools/schedule.py
 F7 ..... <a href="tools/make_audio.py">Synthesize every sound</a> ........ python tools/make_audio.py
 F9 ..... <a href="activities.toml">Load the schedule</a> ............. activities.toml
 F10 .... <a href="tools/render_demo.py">Dev reel, one of everything</a> ... python tools/render_demo.py --dev
 ESC .... Leave ......................... any time. Back with an iced coffee
</pre>

<details>
<summary><b>Order List (F11)</b>: four timers, more than 90 activities, and a great many dots</summary>
<br>

[`activities.toml`](activities.toml) lists more than 90 activities (94 on 2026-10-02, and sessions add more every few hours). Most sit on four timers; the rest are chained follow-ups that only start when something else finishes, like the tide that comes for each sandcastle.

| Timer | Goes off every | In a typical 10-hour run |
| --- | --- | --- |
| regular | 2 to 5 minutes | about 155 |
| occasional | 12 to 25 minutes | about 30 |
| rare | 30 to 60 minutes | about 13 |
| super rare | 3 to 6 hours, at most 3 per run | about 2 |

Typical means the median of 200 simulated runs, plus chained follow-ups. She is busy about a third of the time and idling the rest. Lanes let things overlap, so the sea can be busy while she is: the ship has a habit of choosing exactly that moment. Every start snaps to the next bar of the music (every 3 seconds). The default run is `10:00:00` with seed `1992`, and the same seed gives the same video, event for event. `python tools/schedule.py` validates the file and simulates a run.

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>Instrument List (F4)</b>: twenty of the gags, by their real names</summary>

<pre>
 No  Instrument         Timer       What happens
 01  coconut_sip        regular     Coconut in the shade, eyes closed. Content.
 02  fishing_quiet      regular     Nibbles. Nothing. The usual.
 03  jog_lap            regular     The length of the island and back.
 04  sandcastle         regular     It stands until the tide comes for it.
 05  message_in_bottle  occasional  Thrown. Washes straight back to her feet.
 06  ship_passes_unseen occasional  Crosses the horizon while she is busy.
 07  turtle_visit       occasional  A sea turtle crawls up. Both doze off.
 08  coconut_crab       occasional  Lands on a hermit crab. Then it walks off.
 09  cat_visit          rare        Arrives on a crate. Naps up the palm.
 10  delivery_drone     rare        The parcel is another pair of headphones.
 11  signal_hunt        rare        One bar of signal, at the top of the palm.
 12  shark_nod          rare        In headphones, nodding to the same beat.
 13  tour_boat_selfies  rare        Selfies, her in the background. No lift.
 14  efoil_bro          rare        A shaka from a hydrofoil. He carves off.
 15  fire_by_friction   rare        One curl of smoke, one flame, one wave.
 16  hammock            rare        One palm. No second tree. The raft will do.
 17  lookout            rare        A platform in the crown. The palm bends.
 18  spear_fishing      rare        A heroic lunge, a miss. The gull takes pity.
 19  rescue_almost      super rare  She waves. The ship toots back. Sails on.
 20  leave_any_time     super rare  Walks off over the water. Back with coffee.
</pre>

The bottle gets a reply hours later, in a different bottle. The cat comes back another time. A kumara she plants grows quietly through the rest of the video, and nobody remarks on it.

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>Sample List (F3)</b>: 0 samples, more than 150 sounds made of arithmetic</summary>
<br>

Every sound is synthesized from code in [`tools/make_audio.py`](tools/make_audio.py): no samples, no loops, no recordings, so no third-party licence applies. There are more than 150 sound files so far.

- **Theme:** a seamless 60-second loop at 80 BPM in F major (ii, V, I, vi), 20 bars of exactly 3 seconds: electric piano, a kalimba lead, soft drums and vinyl crackle. Intro, groove, theme and breakdown, then round again.
- **Ocean:** also a seamless 60-second loop.
- **Levels:** the mix sits at -14 LUFS with true peak at or below -1 dBTP, and every level can be set on the master and per routine.

Nobody has listened to it yet, so this list makes no claims about how it sounds.

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>Info Page (F5)</b>: what the screen up there is doing</summary>
<br>

- **The letters are the channels.** C is her, then the cat, the turtle, the sea and sky, the shore, the garden, the theme and the ocean. Each letter is that channel's pattern window, cut to shape, so a note only shows the part that fits. The green dots are empty cells.
- **One row per beat.** A tracker row lasts speed × 2.5 ÷ tempo seconds, so Speed 24 at tempo 80 is one row every 0.75 seconds: the rows step up in time with the theme, every fourth row (a bar line, where activities may start) is tinted, and the whole screen loops every 60 seconds, exactly where the theme does.
- **The minute shown** is staged and squeezed to fit, not captured from a run. It plays instrument 20, `leave_any_time`. The theme channel carries the theme's real chord roots, one per bar, the ocean loop retriggers on row 0, and the theme meter follows the real arrangement. On bar 3 she stands and stretches: one long note at volume 64. On bar 4 she walks off over the water: the volume column falls and her pan dot steps right, out of the window. On bar 8, note off. Channel 01 is then silent for 27 rows, which at one row a beat is the routine's twenty empty seconds, as near as rows allow. On row 55 she walks back in with an iced coffee, sits down and explains nothing.
- **Reduced motion** holds the frame at bar 11: her channel empty, the theme carrying on without her.

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>Song Message (Shift-F9)</b>: greetz and small print</summary>
<br>

Greetz to the cast: the cat (for the naps), the turtle (for the dozing), the shark (for keeping time), the hermit crab (now wearing a coconut), the hydrofoil bro (shaka received), the gull (for the pity fish) and whoever sells iced coffee out there (never explained).

Unhurried Tracker and Copra Software do not exist, and no rows were actually reserved. The screen is an original homage to the DOS text-mode trackers of the 1990s, such as Scream Tracker 3 and Impulse Tracker; no names, fonts or screens were copied from them. Castaway is an unofficial remake inspired by *Johnny Castaway* (1992), which belongs to its owners; its castaway does not appear here.

</details>
